newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of May 26, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - IBM Corp's Lotus Development Corp unit will help Internet Service Providers and their customers usher in a new online collaborative era next month when it ships the first of its "rentable" service provider applications, PC Week reported May 26.
A startup readying new management software that will give business managers more intelligent performance reports about their SAP R/3 applications software, PC Week reported May 26.

COMPUTERWORLD - IBM's Lotus Development Corp will hike the price of its Domino Server software starting July 1 and analysts said that the increase is an attempt by Lotus to make up for falling prices on its client software over the past few years, ComputerWorld reported May 26.

Microsoft Corp's "Scalability Day" last week was short on substance and long on hype, and many users and analysts said that while the demonstrations of the scalability of Windows NT were impressive, they do not translate into real-world situations, Computerworld reported May 26.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Microsoft Corp is setting its sights on yet another UNIX bastion - the telecommunications switch market - and it will lay out plans for a full-fledged Windows NT attack at the upcoming SuperComm conference in New Orleans on June 3, Computer Reseller News reported May 26.

Hewlett-Packard Co will redirect the flow of its high-end business so that 80 percent of its UNIX sales will go through the reseller channel in the next two years and will markedly change HP's sales strategy, CRN reported May 26.

INFOWORLD - IBM is pouring $100 million into its Thomas Watson Research Center this year in order to develop a wide variety of Internet and networking based technologies, some of which will be coming out this year, InfoWorld reported May 26.
IBM's Microelectronics unit will be one of the first entities with a Java accelerator chip, with samples in the fourth quarter or first quarter of 1998, InfoWorld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - International Business Machines Corp's Tivoli Systems division and Sun Microsystems Inc's SunSoft unit are working on a project that would merge their technologies for information management, Information Week reported in its May 26 issue.
Novell Inc is planning a major round of layoffs and is seeking to hire several top executives under new chief executive officer Eric Schmidt, Information Week reported.

EE TIMES - A new blend of Sun Microsystems' Java language, called JavaCard, was developed just for smart cards and promises the ability to use a single smart card for multiple applications, such as electronic cash, credit, debit and buying profile data, EE Times reported May 26.

A breakthrough product called Phantom is spawning a firestrom of activity in the next frontier of three dimensional virtual space: called haptics or "touch" technology, letting users "feel" virtual objects.

Futuristic applications could include virtual circuit boards that designers can manipulate by hand and surgical simulations that let doctors "feel" an organ without making a cut, EE Times reportd in its May 26 issue.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - The year-long meltdown of 64 megabit dynamic random access memory chip prices may be squeezing profit margins for some Japanese chip makers, just as they are cranking up production, EBN reported May 26.
Prices of 64-megabit DRAM chips continued to fall last month, edging closer to those prices for the equivalent amount of 16-megabit parts, according to the EBN Barometer on May 26.

INTERACTIVE WEEK - A little-known trade group is developing a service that will allow small Internet service providers to offer customers toll-free access numbers at fixed costs, making it possible for them to compete with much larger rivals, InterActive Week reported May 26.

Netscape Communications Corp's star is falling as sales of its browsers are slipping and its stock has lost 60 percent of its value in the past year. The question now is can Netscape successfully execute its plan to become a purveyor of enterprise strength systems and services, Interactive Week reported May 26.

MACWEEK - Mac developers may be waiting for Rhapsody but a handful of NeXT Computer's OpenStep veteran developers are racing to ship the first applications for Apple Computer Inc's new operating system, MacWeek reported May 26.
